# calibration error

- **CURIE:** [`gmeow:calibrationError`](gmeow-calibrationError.md)
- **IRI:** <https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/calibrationError>
- **Category:** property
- **Defined by:** [`gmeow:slices/metacognition`](../../slices/metacognition.md)
- **Box roles:** [RBox role](../boxes/rbox.md) ([What is this?](../../four-boxes/index.md))

A SOLVER-LAYER numeric measure of miscalibration ([Principle 12](https://github.com/Blackcat-Informatics/gmeow-ontology/blob/main/CONSTITUTION.md#principle-12)) — a Brier-style score in the closed interval [0,1] attached to the statement asserting a metacognitive calibration, quantifying the gap between avowed confidence and accuracy (0 = perfectly calibrated). An [owl:AnnotationProperty](http://www.w3.org/2002/07/owl#AnnotationProperty) by design, exactly like [`gmeow:confidence`](gmeow-confidence.md): it is INVISIBLE to the reasoner and can never become a materialised axiom, so the calibration metric stays computed-not-asserted. The qualitative direction is [`gmeow:calibration`](gmeow-calibration.md); this is the magnitude.

## Structure

**Property shape:** annotation property

## Practical Pattern

Use [`gmeow:calibrationError`](gmeow-calibrationError.md) when the definition matches the source fact. Prefer a narrower GMEOW term when one exists, and keep projection concerns in the mapping layer.

### Dunning Kruger

- **Source:** [`slices/core/metacognition/examples/dunning-kruger.ttl`](https://github.com/Blackcat-Informatics/gmeow-ontology/blob/main/slices/core/metacognition/examples/dunning-kruger.ttl)
- **Examples catalog:** [open in catalog](../../examples/index.md#example-slices-core-metacognition-examples-dunning-kruger)#example-slices-core-metacognition-examples-dunning-kruger

```turtle
# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: 2026 Blackcat Informatics® Inc. <paudley@blackcatinformatics.ca>
# SPDX-License-Identifier: CC-BY-4.0
#
# Worked example — Dunning–Kruger as a MODELLED metacognitive miscalibration, the
# second-order companion to the cognition slice's dunning-kruger.ttl. Where that
# example records two coexisting first-order gmeow:KnowledgeProficiency claims at
# divergent depths (Principle 9), this one turns the reflexive lens on Sam's OWN
# self-assessment: a gmeow:MetacognitiveState whose gmeow:metaTarget is Sam's
# self-attributed mastery, carrying gmeow:calibration gmeow:overconfident. The
# numeric Brier-style gap rides gmeow:calibrationError — a SOLVER-LAYER annotation
# (Principle 12), invisible to the reasoner. The calibration is itself a
# vantage-indexed claim (Principle 9): the assessor judges Sam overconfident; GMEOW
# records the judgement, it does not adjudicate a global verdict.
@prefix gmeow: <https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/> .
@prefix ex:    <https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/examples/metacognition/> .
@prefix wd:    <http://www.wikidata.org/entity/> .

# --- The calibration is a vantage-indexed claim (Principle 9): the assessor,
#     observing Sam's self-regard against a knows-about assessment, judges it
#     overconfident and records the Brier-style magnitude as a solver-layer
#     annotation on the claim (computed-not-asserted, Principle 12).
ex:samCalibrationClaim a gmeow:StandpointClaim ;
    gmeow:vantage           ex:assessor ;
    gmeow:observedFeature   ex:samSelfRegard ;
    gmeow:observationMethod gmeow:methodExpertJudgement ;
    gmeow:claimModality     gmeow:probable ;
    gmeow:calibrationError  0.62 .
```

## Usage Advice

### Use when

- Use to attach a solver-computed Brier-style miscalibration magnitude in [0,1] to the statement that asserts a metacognitive calibration, when the numeric error is worth recording alongside the qualitative [`gmeow:calibration`](gmeow-calibration.md).

### Avoid when

- Avoid modelling it as an [owl:DatatypeProperty](http://www.w3.org/2002/07/owl#DatatypeProperty) with a domain — that would make it a reasoned ABox edge and risk the reasoner touching it, violating the solver boundary ([Principle 12](https://github.com/Blackcat-Informatics/gmeow-ontology/blob/main/CONSTITUTION.md#principle-12)) — and avoid deriving any entailment from it; it is recorded structure, not logic.

### How to use

- Attach [`gmeow:calibrationError`](gmeow-calibrationError.md) as an annotation on the calibration statement (the reified claim or the triple), carrying the externally-computed Brier-style value in [0,1]; leave its computation entirely to the solver layer.

### Examples

- ex:samCalibrationClaim [`gmeow:calibrationError`](gmeow-calibrationError.md) 0.62.
